title: NSGA-III — the complete algorithm sourcebook
sourceEncoding: UTF-8; content preserves original BOM, line endings and trailing newline
lineCountConvention: Physical lines; a terminal line break does not add an extra empty line. Blank lines within a file count.
symbolIndexConvention: Top-level member declarations in the current repository formatting; nested members may be unindexed. All source remains present.
callGraphConvention: Curated local calls, with default delegate and NSGAIIISampler virtual dispatch explicitly labeled. External runtime calls and custom strategy overrides are outside this graph.

boundary.included: Every line of NSGAIIISampler, NSGAIIIElitePopulationSelectionStrategy, BaseGASampler, BaseSampler (including constraint post-processing), RandomSampler, LazyRandomState, the entire shared Nsgaii subtree, nondominated sorting, constraint evaluation, intersection and conditional search spaces, transforms, distributions, ordered dictionaries, and the listed numerical/formatting support files.
excluded: Study, Trial, FrozenTrial, Optuna entry points, trial states/directions, objective evaluation, optimization orchestration, storage implementations, logging, project/assembly setup, and other OptunaSharp framework services.
NumSharp NDArray, NumPyRandom/MT19937 implementation, NumSharp exceptions, NumSharp.Interop.OpenBLAS, native BLAS/LAPACK, .NET runtime/BCL, and their transitive dependencies.
Other samplers (including NSGAIISampler itself), tests, the upstream Python implementation, and this presentation host/JavaScript; these are not the NSGA-III algorithm source bundle.
notes: Whole files are included even when only one method is used by NSGA-III. In particular NSGA-II crowding-distance selection is present because the same file supplies RankPopulation; NSGA-III does not invoke that crowding-distance path.

The default sampler creates UniformCrossover and mutates by independent resampling. The presentation host configures SBXCrossover and PolynomialMutation; both full operator implementations are included.
ConditionalParams is an opt-in OptunaSharp extension. It preserves eligible conditional parameters for evolution; its disabled path retains the standard intersection-space behavior.
Source comments are reproduced as written, including historical parity statements. This source archive is not a new claim that every comment has been independently verified.

The presentation replays a real completed backend generation. Diagnostic stages and highlighted methods explain those results; they are not instruction-level debugger stepping or a live CPU program counter.

The eight stages form a teaching-level flow graph. Objective evaluation happens in Study/the user objective outside this archive; member ranges link the actual implementation responsible for each step.

symbols.summary: After replacing infinities, subtract the ideal point, find ASF extreme points, and solve the extreme-point hyperplane. A degenerate matrix uses per-axis maxima instead. The selection set contains accepted fronts plus the borderline front.

symbols.summary: Associate every normalized individual with the reference line having minimum perpendicular distance. Exact ties keep the first reference row.

stages.title: Initialize a population
stages.summary: Initial parameters are sampled independently within their distributions. Study evaluates each suggested trial; the sampler does not evaluate the objective.

stages.title: Breed and mutate
stages.summary: Dominance tournaments select parents. The configured crossover produces a child, or one parent is copied. Parameters mutate with the configured probability; absent proposals use independent sampling.
stages.formula: Qₜ = evaluate(mutate(crossover(Pₜ))); pₘ = configured value or 1 / max(1, n_params)

stages.title: Combine parents and offspring
stages.summary: SelectParent gathers the previous generation and its cached parent population, then invokes the NSGA-III elite strategy.

stages.title: Sort by nondomination
stages.summary: Ranking converts maximization objectives to losses and applies nondominated sorting. When constrained, feasible trials precede infeasible trials ranked by total positive violation.
stages.formula: a ≺ b ⇔ (∀j: aⱼ ≤ bⱼ) ∧ (∃j: aⱼ < bⱼ); Rₜ → F₀, F₁, …

stages.title: Normalize the selection set
stages.summary: After replacing infinities, subtract the ideal point, find ASF extreme points, and solve the extreme-point hyperplane. A degenerate matrix uses per-axis maxima instead. The selection set contains accepted fronts plus the borderline front.
stages.formula: zⱼ = minᵢ fᵢⱼ; Eα = 1; yᵢⱼ = (fᵢⱼ − zⱼ) αⱼ

stages.title: Associate with a reference direction
stages.summary: Associate every normalized individual with the reference line having minimum perpendicular distance. Exact ties keep the first reference row.
stages.formula: πᵣ(y) = ((y · r) / ‖r‖²) r; d(y,r) = ‖y − πᵣ(y)‖; r* = argminᵣ d(y,r)

stages.title: Fill the least occupied niches
stages.summary: Only accepted fronts initially contribute occupancy. Among reference directions with borderline candidates, choose a least occupied direction. An empty niche takes its nearest candidate; a populated niche uses the sampler’s shuffled order.
stages.formula: r* ∈ argminᵣ ρᵣ; ρᵣ = 0 ⇒ nearest candidate; ρᵣ > 0 ⇒ shuffled candidate; ρᵣ ← ρᵣ + 1
variables: ρᵣ: selected occupancy of direction r
borderline: front that reaches or exceeds N

stages.title: Keep the next parent population
stages.summary: Append the niche-selected members to all accepted earlier fronts and return the elite population. BaseGASampler caches these parents for subsequent child generation.
stages.formula: Pₜ₊₁ = accepted fronts ∪ niche-selected members; |Pₜ₊₁| = N
variables: N: target size, when enough completed candidates exist
